title: Otello
facts: Otello premiered at La Scala, Milan, on 5 February 1887 and was a resounding success.
The first-night audience called Verdi back for 20 curtain calls at the end of the opera.
After Aida (1871) Verdi retired from opera. It took his publisher Ricordi about ten years to coax him into even looking at Boito’s libretto.
For three Christmases in a row Ricordi sent Verdi a cake topped with a chocolate figure of the Moor. The secret project was nicknamed “chocolate”.
Boito proposed Iago’s “a sort of evil Credo”. Verdi’s verdict: “Most beautiful this Credo; most powerful and wholly Shakespearian.”
With “Esultate!” Verdi “hit upon the precise form of one of the most famous entrances in all opera.”
Preparations for the premiere were held in absolute secrecy, and Verdi kept the right to cancel it up to the last minute.
Verdi only settled on the title in a letter to Boito: “I would find it hypocritical not to call it Otello.”
Enrico Caruso was studying Otello when he died in 1921, ending the Met’s plans to stage it for its star tenor.
Plácido Domingo: when he decided to sing Otello, “many people told me that I was crazy” because his voice was nothing like Mario Del Monaco’s.
Plácido Domingo, My First Forty Years (via Wikipedia)
Even the first Otello, Francesco Tamagno, didn’t fully satisfy Verdi: a letter to his publisher says Tamagno “left a great deal to be desired”.
For years white singers wore dark makeup as Otello. The Met stopped the practice in 2015.
